120	Now, after we have seen the Torah and the verse
121	in the Writings, in the book of Kohelet, let's see the Mishnah
122	in tractate Bava
123	Metsia, chapter 4 of Bava Metsia, it is written as follows:
124	If he pulled the fruit from him but did not give him the money, he cannot
125	retract. If he gave him the money but did not pull the fruit,
126	he can retract. But they said: He who punished the people of the generation
127	of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion will in the future punish the one
128	who does not stand by his word. Let's try to understand this.
129	First of all, let's study only the topic there in tractate Bava
130	Metsia.
131	Tractate Bava Metsia is the middle tractate between
132	two other tractates, Bava Kamma and Bava Batra. These three
133	tractates, Bava Kamma, Bava Metsia and Bava Batra,
134	make up a larger tractate called Nezikin,
135	which is actually an order, and it is found in the order
136	of Nezikin, among the six orders of the Mishnah in the Talmud.
137	And these tractates deal with matters
138	of monetary law. In chapter 4 of Bava Metsia it speaks about
139	the system of acquisitions, how one acquires things. That is, there are
140	objects that are mine, property that is mine,
141	and the question is how an asset becomes mine or
142	leaves my possession. Now, here it speaks about two
143	people in the discussion here
144	in the Mishnah,
145	where one sells fruit to another,
146	say a greengrocer or a fruit seller
147	in the market. The fruit is, of course, not yet his, and now
148	a buyer comes and wants to buy. So you need to know that
149	when buying fruit, the acquisition is not made by payment of
150	the money, as is commonly thought today, but rather
151	the acquisition is made by means of
152	pulling. That is, from the moment the buyer pulled the item
153	that he is buying, in this case fruit, from
154	the seller's possession, he pulled it, meaning he attached it to himself,
155	this is what creates the acquisition, even if he has not yet
156	paid the
157	money. Let me give an example. Imagine a person
158	enters not a shop where fruit and vegetables are bought,
159	but he goes to buy a vase or some
160	glassware, right? So there is the display
161	in the shop, and he says to the seller: I want the
162	third vase there on the second shelf from the
163	right. The seller goes and takes down
164	this one,
165	and the vase falls
166	and breaks, even if he paid the
167	money. The customer, as if, only has to be brought
168	this one. The payment of the money does not make the acquisition until
169	the vase actually reaches his possession. That is, what
170	makes the acquisition here is
171	the pulling. Now, after more or less this principle,
172	let's see the Mishnah again: If he pulled the fruit from him and did not give him
173	the money.
174	They agreed that he buys from him, I don't know how many,
175	ten crates of oranges or apples, I don't know
176	what, and the customer pulled the fruit from the shop
177	owner and still did not give him the money. He has not yet paid him.
178	He only pulled and did not pay the money, and afterwards he wants
179	to retract. He says, you know what, no, I don't
180	want the fruit, it is not good, I am not buying it. But he already pulled it. The shop owner can say
181	to him:
182	I'm sorry, you pulled it, it is already yours, I am not willing to take
183	it back. This is the meaning of "he pulled fruit from him and did not
184	give him the money, he cannot retract." If he gave him the
185	money but did not pull fruit from him, that is, they
186	agreed that he buys these crates of oranges
187	and he already paid him the money but has not yet
188	pulled it, he can retract,
189	because there was no acquisition here. What is the determining acquisition?
190	It is the acquisition by pulling. Now, what happens here? To this
191	the Mishnah refers and says: But they said, He who punished
192	the people of the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion will in the future
193	punish the one who does not stand by his word. That is,
194	you committed yourself, true, you have not yet carried out the acquisition, but
195	you committed yourself. So by strict law you can retract.
196	But know that it is a serious matter, what is written here: He who
197	punished the people of the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion
198	will in the future punish the one who does not stand by his word. The generation
199	of the Flood is the story that appears at the end of the book, at the end
200	of Parashat Bereshit, the beginning of Parashat Noach, right: All flesh
201	had corrupted its way upon the earth, and I am destroying them from the earth,
202	and the Flood came
203	and actually destroyed all
204	that lived. The people of the generation of the Flood were wicked people,
205	and the Holy One, blessed be He, destroyed them. Ten generations
206	later they built the Tower of Babel. This is the generation of the Dispersion, in which
207	at first the whole earth was of one language and one speech,
208	and then the Holy One, blessed be He, confounded their language, and this is called
209	Dispersion, He divided
210	them. And this punishment of the generation of the Flood and of the generation
211	of the Dispersion is the punishment of a person who does not stand
212	by his word. And here note that the Mishnah is not speaking
213	about matters between man and God, it is speaking about matters between
214	man and his fellow, about a commercial commitment,
215	by speech, by speech. So it is true that apparently there was no
216	pulling here, and therefore the shop owner cannot
217	say to him, listen, you pulled it, it is yours.
218	He can retract. But if he retracts,
219	he is in effect breaking his word, breaking his own word.
220	One who breaks his word, it is written here, something very
221	serious, that he is destined to end up as the people of the generation
222	of the Flood and the people of the generation of the Dispersion ended. And one must know that these matters
223	are not trivial. One must understand what happened
224	in the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion that is connected to the matter of
225	not standing
226	by one's word.
227	What all this shows us is that speech is something very, very
228	serious. We came out of this, remember this whole journey,
229	we started from the verses in the Torah, the three verses in the Torah,
230	in the book of Devarim, in our parashah, Parashat Ki Tetzê: When
231	you vow a vow to HaShem, do not delay to pay it, and so on.
232	We saw the verses also in Kohelet, we saw now
233	this Mishnah in Bava Metsia, and now let's
234	try to go a bit deeper. Perhaps we begin with the matter
235	of what is the connection between standing by one's word and the terrible punishment
236	that appears here, which is parallel to the generation
237	of the Flood and the generation of the
238	Dispersion. So for this purpose, let's go to the book of Bereshit.
